metadata.case_name: TSANG CHUNG WAN v. LI MING AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_after: casual construction worker at Chek Lap Kok

injuries.description: comminuted fracture of the proximal phalanx of his right ring finger
source: As a result of the accident, The Plaintiff, who is right handed, suffered a comminuted fracture of the proximal phalanx of his right ring finger. It was operated on the same day and K-wire fixation performed.

injuries.description: skin grafting to right middle finger
source: Skin grafting was performed on his right middle finger on 19th October 1993.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified open wound of finger or thumb

injuries.description: proximal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger ankylosed (total loss of range of motion)
injuries.body_part: proximal interphalangeal joint, right ring finger
source: Dr. Chiang found that the Plaintiff's proximal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger to be ankylosed i.e. total loss of range of motion.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the wrist or hand

injuries.description: significant stiffness in the distal interphalangeal joints of the right middle and ring fingers and the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right middle finger
source: He further found that there was significant stiffness in the distal interphalangeal joints of the right middle and ring fingers and the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right middle finger.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the wrist or hand

manifestations.description: total loss of range of motion of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger (ankylosed)
significant stiffness in the distal interphalangeal joints of the right middle and ring fingers and the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right middle finger
pain and stiffness in the ring and middle fingers of his right hand
weakened right hand grip, unable to grasp heavy objects
the loss in motion of the joints of the right middle and ring fingers will cause impairment in performing a full grip as well as the fine and repetitive use of the right hand
permanent impairment assessed at 12% of the whole person by Dr. Arthur Chiang (October 1995); re-assessed at 9% (September 1997); assessed at 8% by Dr. Danny Tsoi (March 1997)

losses.description: the loss in motion of the joints of the right middle and ring fingers will cause impairment in performing a full grip as well as the fine and repetitive use of the right hand
Dr. Chiang concluded that the loss of function of the Plaintiff's right hand was such that it would not be suitable for the Plaintiff to return to his pre-accident work in formwork
